festivals: Thakurani Yatra (biennial, in the month of Chaitra — the month-long Ghata Yatra)

history.dynasty: Cult origin c. 1672 AD per historians — CONFLICT: some sources claim 15th century
history.summary: Maa Budhi Thakurani is the presiding deity (istadevi) of Berhampur and the cultural cornerstone of the city. The cult originated with the Telugu Dera (weaver) community who migrated from Rajahmundry (Andhra Pradesh) at the invitation of the Raja Saheb of Mahuri around 1672 AD — though some sources instead place the origin in the 15th century (CONFLICT). The temple near the Big Bazaar/Bada Bazaar area of old Berhampur is unique for the close association between lower-caste devotees and mainstream Hinduism: the priests are of the barber (Nari/Barik) caste while devotees come from all castes. The deity — described variously as a crude stone idol or a wooden idol smeared with sindoor (CONFLICT) — is conceived as a married daughter who visits her father's house (Desi Behera) once every two years; the nearly month-long Thakurani (Ghata) Yatra in Chaitra celebrates this homecoming, with Bagha Nacha (tiger dance), veshas and giant Raths among its attractions.

name: Maa Budhi Thakurani Temple
town_description: Berhampur (Brahmapur), in Ganjam district of southern Odisha, is the largest city of the region and is popularly known as the 'Silk City' of Odisha. It is the commercial centre of south Odisha and is famous for its biennial Thakurani Yatra, the month-long festival of its presiding deity Maa Budhi Thakurani. The city lies close to the Andhra Pradesh border and to Gopalpur-on-Sea, and is well connected by road and rail.
